target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures describe the company's short-term and long-term funding requirements, specifically covering capital expenditures for manufacturing/assembly/test, process technology investments, and working capital. The 2025 disclosure explicitly mirrors the 2024 structure and content, though with updated restructuring plan references and additional items like pending acquisitions.

The 2024 disclosure details specific long-term investment plans including expansions in Arizona, New Mexico, Oregon, and a new facility in Ohio. The 2025 disclosure (intc_2025_7_D068) contains identical planning details ('These plans include expanding existing operations in Arizona, New Mexico and Oregon and investing in a new leading-edge manufacturing facility in Ohio in the long term'). Although intc_2025_7_D068 also covers short-term funding, its long-term components directly match intc_2024_7_D100's specific subject matter.

comparisons.peer_summary: Liquidity needs primarily stem from working capital, R&D, capital expenditures, dividends, taxes, and payments on $69,847 million of outstanding indebtedness, with capital expenditures expected to be higher in fiscal 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose their short-term and long-term liquidity requirements, highlighting manufacturing and technology investments as key drivers. Intel explicitly lists capital expenditures for manufacturing, process technology, and restructuring costs in its short-term funding, while Broadcom includes working capital, R&D, capital expenditures, and debt service on $69,847 million of indebtedness. Both companies note higher capital expenditures in fiscal 2025, though Broadcom specifies an increase compared to 2024, whereas Intel references significant manufacturing expansion plans incrementally in long-term requirements.

sentences.text: Our short-term funding requirements include capital expenditures for worldwide manufacturing and assembly and test, including investments in our process technology roadmap; investments in our product roadmap; working capital requirements, including cash outlays associated with the 2024 Restructuring Plan; partner distributions to our non-controlling interest holders; and strategic investments.
Our long-term funding requirements incrementally contemplate investments in significant manufacturing expansion plans and investments to accelerate our process technology.

Our short-term and long-term liquidity requirements primarily arise from: (i) business acquisitions and investments we may make from time to time, (ii) working capital requirements, (iii) research and development and capital expenditure needs, (iv) cash dividend payments (if and when declared by our Board of Directors), (v) interest and principal payments related to our $69,847 million of outstanding indebtedness, and (vi) payment of income taxes.
We expect capital expenditures to be higher in the fiscal year ending November 2, 2025 as compared to fiscal year 2024.
